votes.evidence:
The finding holds, but it is minor. It only affects documentation.

- **What the help text says:** In `/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py`, lines 50-54, `stamphog_connected` says that when it is false, "the UI renders it disabled". The help text states no exception.
- **What the UI does:** In `/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx`, lines 1063-1068, the Stamphog `LemonSwitch` sets the Stamphog disabled reason only when `settings && !settings.stamphog_connected && !settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. So if the project is disconnected and the toggle is already on, the switch can still be clicked. Only the shared `switchDisabledReason` can disable it then.

- **Result:** The serializer help text feeds the generated OpenAPI schema and the MCP tool descriptions. For the case "disconnected and already on", it describes a disabled switch that the UI never shows.

votes.evidence:
The help_text and the UI do not match, as the finding says.

- **help_text:** products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:50-54 says that when `stamphog_connected` is false, "the UI renders it disabled with a pointer to connect the Stamphog GitHub App". It does not name an exception.
- **UI:** products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1063-1068 disables the switch only when `!settings.stamphog_connected && !settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. The code comment there says an already-on switch stays interactive so the user can always opt out. On a disconnected project with the toggle already on, the switch is interactive, not disabled.
- **Where the text spreads:** the same sentence appears in products/review_hog/frontend/generated/api.schemas.ts:464 and in services/mcp/src/api/generated.ts:48074 and :56500. API and MCP readers therefore see a description that is wrong for the toggle-on case.

I looked for tests or guards that would cover this and found none. No test checks help_text, and nothing ties the help_text to the frontend condition. No code path makes the help_text accurate for the toggle-on, disconnected case.

The blast radius is small. The field is read-only and computed. The text is documentation about UI rendering, not about API behavior. Nothing is lost or computed wrongly. A one-line wording fix resolves it.

votes.evidence:
The finding is real but minor, so I rated it "consider".

- **What the help text says:** products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:50-54 says that when stamphog_connected is false, "the UI renders it disabled with a pointer to connect the Stamphog GitHub App". There is no exception for a toggle that is already on.
- **What the UI does:** products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx, around lines 1061-1068, sets the Stamphog switch's disabledReason only when `settings && !settings.stamphog_connected && !settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. If the toggle is already on, the switch falls back to switchDisabledReason and stays clickable. A comment there says this is deliberate: "An already-on switch stays interactive while disconnected".
- **Can production reach this case?** Yes. A user turns the toggle on while a synced, enabled Stamphog repository exists. Later that repository is disabled or removed, so stamphog_connected becomes false. The saved stamphog_review_inbox_prs=true stays, and the switch renders enabled. That contradicts the help text.
- **Why it matters a little:** the help text becomes the field description in the generated OpenAPI schema, and from there in the generated TS and MCP tool descriptions. API consumers get a slightly wrong description of the UI.
votes.refutation:
I tried three ways to refute it, and none worked.
1. I looked for a backend guard that turns the toggle off when the project disconnects. The serializer has none; it only reports stamphog_connected. So the on-while-disconnected state can happen.
2. I checked whether the frontend disables the switch in every disconnected case. It does not: the disabled condition explicitly requires the toggle to be off.
3. The first half of the help text ("has nothing to act on") is still accurate. Only the claim that the UI always disables the switch is wrong.

This is a documentation error only. Runtime behavior is correct and the user can still opt out, so the impact is small.
